triage.note: D7, both halves of the postmortem's trust amplifier. PANEL: `doc_status` and the warnings list live in the top banner and the side panel showed `conf 0.95` beside neither — postmortem §2, 'during a demo, the panel is the product'. Pinned as an ADJACENCY rather than as a question about the file: every live interpolation of `it.confidence` must sit where the pinned marker would start and must be followed IMMEDIATELY by `${docQual()}${itemQual(it)}`. PR #53 R2/R4 corrected this sentence, which used to end 'so a bare number is unrepresentable': three of that round's six findings were attacks straight through that word. The adjacency alone proved nothing about whether the qualifier RUNS (an early `if(true) return "";` left every pinned line intact below it as dead code and passed), nor about whether the banner strip is ever CALLED, nor about a site spelled `confidence ${it.confidence ?? "—"}` that the old literal `conf ${` scan could not see. So the three helper bodies are now pinned WHOLE via `bodies`, the call is pinned inside the banner assignment that makes it, and the scan looks for the FIELD rather than for one spelling of its label. The `boilerplate_plumbing` allow-list records why (PR #27 R5/R6): a question about a hop is answerable by a broken hop, and a list of forbidden shapes only bans the ones someone already thought of. `min_conf_sites` 2 is the anti-vacuity floor — the sidebar badge and the pane header each print one, and deleting a site is not a way to qualify it. The wire pins fix WHAT the qualifier reads: the response's own `doc_status` (the same read-at-request-time rule S8 gave the pane header) and the item's own `evidence.warnings`, which IS validate.py `score()`'s `hits` list, so the panel names exactly the codes that cost this item WARN_PENALTY and inherits ADR-018's exclusion of `expected_item_missing` instead of re-deriving a second definition in the display layer. BANNER: `unattributed_content` already computes the document-coverage figure and buries it in a warning row (postmortem §8 gap 1); `coverageStrip` surfaces it in the banner with validate.py's own caveat attached. `must_not_say` forbids the inversion that caveat exists to prevent — interior gaps are NOT counted, so `100 - outside` is not the attributed share and a banner publishing it would overstate coverage by exactly the uncounted gaps. Display layer only: `extract_items` output is untouched and the envelope half (a coverage field plus an escalation threshold) is D8's row. PR #53 R3 also split the badge class: `lo` keeps its pre-D7 meaning (amber TEXT = this item's own validators fired) and the document-level qualifier gets `docw` (amber BORDER), because folding both into `lo` repainted all 23 jpm-2024 badges identically and erased the one signal that finds item 15. The `flag` expression is a wire pin so that split is a pinned decision rather than an incidental one. PR #53 R7 renamed the banner label from 'document coverage:' to 'unattributed content:' — the figure measures NON-coverage, and a label reading 'coverage' over a bolded 73% is the same inversion `must_not_say` already forbids in arithmetic form; the old label is now itself forbidden.
triage.ceiling: STATIC READ. This check parses the MARKUP TEXT of src/sec10k/web/static/index.html — no test in this harness issues an HTTP request, so it does NOT observe the render. WHAT IT GUARANTEES (narrowed to the truth at PR #53 R2/R4): no live interpolation of `it.confidence` renders without the pinned qualifier concatenated onto it; the three helpers that produce the qualifier and the banner line are byte-equal to their pinned bodies, so a pinned line cannot sit unreachable below an early return; the banner's call to the strip is pinned in the assignment that makes it; and the badge-class expression is pinned. WHAT IT DOES NOT: a render site that never names `it.confidence` — one that copies the number into a local first, or reads it off a re-shaped object — is outside the scan entirely, and `min_conf_sites` does not help, since the two legitimate sites already satisfy the floor. Nor can it see any of this reach a screen: a CSS rule (`#coverage{display:none}`) keeps every pin here green while the banner says nothing, the same pin-mechanism hole `ui-exclusion-note`'s ceiling states, on a new element. It also cannot see the figure itself — `coverageStrip` only fires when `unattributed_content` fired, i.e. only above UNATTRIBUTED_MAX, so a document at 20% non-coverage shows no line at all. That is deliberate: the figure would have to be computed to be shown, and computing one in the display layer is the envelope change D8 owns. Render evidence is in tasks/reviews/d7-browser-walk.json; the isolating falsification runs are in tasks/reviews/pr53_mutation_probe.py.
